{"content": "### Configure OpenCode using opencode.jsonc

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx

Example configuration file in JSONC format specifying the schema, default model, auto-update preference, and server port. OpenCode supports both standard JSON and JSONC formats.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",
  "autoupdate": true,
  "server": {
    "port": 4096,
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR overrides global config path

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/global.ts

When OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is set, it replaces the default XDG config path (~/.config/opencode) used as the global config directory. All global config files (config.json, opencode.json, opencode.jsonc) are loaded from this directory instead.

```typescript
    config: Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR ?? Path.config,
```

--------------------------------

### Configuration precedence and locations

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/core/src/config.ts

Config loading walks up from the opened directory to the project root discovering .opencode dirs and config files. Documents are ordered lowest-to-highest priority: global config → project files → .opencode files. The global config directory defaults to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode and is overridable via OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR. Policy rules are loaded in reverse order so user-global rules override repository rules.

```typescript
const globalDirectory = AbsolutePath.make(global.config)
const locationIsGlobal = path.resolve(location.directory) === path.resolve(global.config)
const discovered = locationIsGlobal
  ? []
  : yield* fs
      .up({
        targets: [".opencode", ...names.toReversed()],
        start: location.directory,
        stop: location.project.directory,
      })
      .pipe(Effect.orDie)
const directories = [
  globalDirectory,
  ...discovered
    .filter((item) => path.basename(item) === ".opencode")
    .toReversed()
    .map((directory) => AbsolutePath.make(directory)),
]
const directPaths = discovered.filter((item) => path.basename(item) !== ".opencode").toReversed()
const direct = yield* Effect.forEach(directPaths, loadFile)
const supplementary = yield* Effect.forEach(directories, loadDirectory)
// Apply general settings first and more specific settings last:
// global config, project files, then `.opencode` files.
const configs = [...(supplementary[0] ?? []), ...direct, ...supplementary.slice(1).flat()]
// Rules use the opposite order so a user-global rule can override a
// repository rule.
yield* policy.load(
  configs
    .filter((config): config is Document => config.type === "document")
    .toReversed()
    .flatMap((config) => config.info.experimental?.policies ?? []),
)
```

--------------------------------

### OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT provides inline config, skipping global file creation

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts

When OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (or OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR) is set, the global config file with the $schema is NOT auto-created. The content is parsed as JSON and merged as a 'local' source after project configs but before remote account config.

```typescript
      if (!Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG && !Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR && !Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT) {
        const file = globalConfigFile()
        if (!existsSync(file)) {
          yield* fs
            .writeWithDirs(file, JSON.stringify({ $schema: "https://opencode.ai/config.json" }, null, 2))
            .pipe(Effect.catch(() => Effect.void))
        }
      }
```

--------------------------------

### OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is appended to config discovery paths

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/config/paths.ts

OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is added as an additional config directory alongside .opencode directories during config discovery. In TUI config loading, it's treated equivalently to .opencode directories.

```typescript
    ...(Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR ? [Flag.OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR] : []),
```", "results": []}
